advisory_open_decisions.question: Which character encoding (code page) do the files and areas described by these copybooks use for DISPLAY data on the legacy platform (EBCDIC 037, 1140, another EBCDIC variant, or ASCII)? The zoned-decimal test vectors and String codecs depend on it.

RTNCDE00 uses 5 PERFORM ... THRU ranges (each Pn00 THRU Pn00-EXIT) and BR-041 (time-window analysis: COUNT, MAX and MIN of RETURN_CODE for one program with TIMESTAMP between start and end inclusive) is medium confidence. Confirm the inclusive time-window semantics and that the THRU ranges carry no behaviour beyond their single paragraph.

RTNANA00 and RTNCDE00 include SQLCA (a self-including copybook) inside a program 01 WS-DB2-AREA, so the copybook's 01 SQL-STATUS-CODES record is nested under another 01, and SQLCODE/SQLERRMC have no Field ID. Should the Java design model WS-DB2-AREA as the SQLCA copybook record (35 bytes) or replace it entirely with JDBC SQLException/SQLState handling?

RTNCDE00's caller interface RC-REQUEST-AREA (165 bytes) consists only of the 01 record of copybook RTNCODE (SYS-PORTFOLIO-001-FIL-0013-REC-0001) nested inside another 01. Is the RTNCODE copybook record (mapped in the RTNCODE unit's packet) the authoritative interface contract for all callers of RTNCDE00?

requirements.statement: The return-code service selects its action from the request type (RC-REQUEST-TYPE): 'I' initialises the return-code area (program ID spaces, current and highest code 0, status SUCCESS, response code 0); 'S' records a new return code; 'G' returns the current code, the highest code and the status with response code 0; 'L' inserts one row into DB2 table RTNCODES with the current timestamp, program ID, current code, highest code, status and message, setting response code 0 when the insert succeeds (SQLCODE 0) and 8 otherwise; 'A' analyses logged codes over a time window. Any other request type performs nothing and leaves the response code unchanged.

evidence.by: deterministic claim check of the cited statement

independent_portion.text: EXEC SQL INSERT INTO RTNCODES (TIMESTAMP, PROGRAM_ID, RETURN_CODE, HIGHEST_CODE, STATUS_CODE, MESSAGE_TEXT) VALUES (:WS-CURRENT-TIME, :RC-PROGRAM-ID, :RC-CURRENT-CODE, :RC-HIGHEST-CODE, :RC-STATUS, :RC-MESSAGE) END-EXEC.

EXEC SQL SELECT COUNT(*), MAX(RETURN_CODE), MIN(RETURN_CODE) INTO :RC-TOTAL-CODES, :RC-MAX-CODE, :RC-MIN-CODE FROM RTNCODES WHERE PROGRAM_ID = :RC-PROGRAM-ID AND TIMESTAMP >= :RC-START-TIME AND TIMESTAMP <= :RC-END-TIME END-EXEC.

requirements.statement: When a new return code is set ('S'), if it is greater than the highest code recorded so far (RC-HIGHEST-CODE) it becomes the new highest code; otherwise the highest code is kept. In both cases the current code becomes the new code. The highest code is held in the caller's request area, so it persists only as long as the caller keeps that area.

requirements.statement: On an analyse request ('A') the system counts the logged return codes in RTNCODES for the requested program ID whose timestamp is greater than or equal to the caller's start time and less than or equal to the caller's end time, and returns the count, the highest (MAX) and the lowest (MIN) logged return code. The response code is 0 when the query succeeds (SQLCODE 0) and 8 otherwise.
